name: Globus Spirits Ltd
title: Globus Spirits Ltd - 533104 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Globus Spirits Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR7,888 million, EBITDA up 33% to INR795 million, PAT up 49% to INR276 million (corrected figures).
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong growth across manufacturing and consumer, with EBITDA margin of about 10% and PAT margin of about 4%. Manufacturing (ENA/ethanol) volumes reached 56.11 million litres at a record 89% utilisation, with EBITDA of about INR6.5 per litre within the INR5-7 guidance band. Prestige and above (P&A) revenue grew 35% YoY to INR550 million but still posted negative EBITDA of INR13 million, while Regular and Others (R&O) grew 10% with UP volumes scaling rapidly. Management flagged glass and PET cost-push of 10-17% and seasonal agri inflation in Q2, but said it is hedged within the margin band. Net debt was INR650 crore versus INR660 crore in March 2026. Several figures were corrected during the call: revenue should read INR7,888 million, PAT INR276 million and growth 49%, and EBITDA per litre INR6.5.

INR276 million (corrected from INR278 million stated on call)
INR6.5 (corrected from INR6.6 stated on call)

segments.name: Manufacturing (ENA/ethanol)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11% YoY to INR4,720 million on 56.11 million litres sold, with 89% capacity utilisation on about 334 million litres installed capacity. EBITDA was about INR6.5 per litre, within the INR5-7 guidance band.

segments.name: Prestige and above (P&A)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 35% YoY and 38% QoQ to INR550 million, with volumes up 45% YoY to 0.42 million cases. EBITDA was negative INR13 million as spending went into distribution and brand building; brands cited were Terai, Snoski and Brothers & Co.

segments.name: Regular and Others (R&O)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10% YoY to INR2,564 million, volumes up 13% YoY to 4.48 million cases and EBITDA up 13% YoY to INR440 million. UP R&O volumes grew 2.4x YoY and crossed 0.2 million cases per month.

guidance_outlook: Manufacturing EBITDA guided at INR5-7 per litre; management expects to stay in this range for all quarters of FY27.
R&O EBITDA margin guidance of 15-17%, with mix from lower-margin UP expected to pull margins toward 15-16% from the 17-18% of recent years.
Maintenance capex of about INR50-60 crore a year; no new ENA/ethanol capacity planned, with at most about 1% gain from technology. No capacity expansion planned through FY29.
P&A expected to reach profitability sooner rather than later, having moved from about negative 60% margin a couple of years ago to near breakeven.
Management expects the UK FTA to benefit the industry on Scotch costs, but said the timing and size of the benefit are uncertain and not yet visible in numbers.
West Bengal R&O re-entry expected within about 60 days of regulatory approvals, which management hopes come this quarter.
capex_capacity: Installed manufacturing capacity is about 334 million litres; Q1 utilisation was 89% against a guidance of about 85%.
UP plant utilisation was above 90% in Q1 per the CFO. About 25% of UP output is consumed captively and the rest sold in bulk, with optimisation still under way.
Capex has been limited to maintenance after UP commissioning; cash generation is being fed into P&A growth and debt paydown.
Management expects a 15-17% R&O margin band to hold while UP grows fast.
demand_pricing: Management expects ethanol demand for E20 blending to grow about 7-7.5% a year, in line with petrol growth; E85/E50 depends on car compatibility, which is limited for now.
Industry ethanol is in oversupply, but Globus ran at 89% by shifting ENA and ethanol mix and selling ENA in India and overseas, with overseas prices firming.
Glass and PET cost-push is 10-17% depending on brand and pack and is expected to persist; management says the company holds only slim packaging inventory.
Agri inflation is seasonal: Q2 and part of Q3 are inflationary, then prices ease as harvests arrive. Maize is partly hedged and FCI supplies a fixed-price portion; broken rice is unhedged.
UP is a large market of about 95 lakh cases a month. West Bengal IMIL is about 26-27 lakh cases a month, per management, slightly smaller than Rajasthan or Haryana.
Management says the company has 11 states total presence, with 4 core states plus Delhi and UP (5 core states overall), and a 6th state nearing core status.

qa_highlights.question: How will ethanol demand drivers develop given the E20 controversy, and could ethanol for cooking matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said E20 is government policy, the controversy has not hurt offtake, and demand is growing about 7.5% YoY with sticky month-on-month volumes. Cooking-fuel ethanol adoption will be slow in India without distribution and canisters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expecting Bihar prohibition to be lifted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes prohibition in Bihar will eventually be reversed, but gave no firm timeline, estimating a change over about 1-2 years under the new Chief Minister.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of glass cost inflation on R&O and P&A?
qa_highlights.answer: Glass and PET cost-push is 10-17% by brand and pack and is expected to persist for some time, with energy costs also rising.

qa_highlights.question: Will UK FTA lower Scotch costs and expand gross profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a tailwind as inventory transitions, but benefits depend on suppliers revising base prices. Rupee depreciation of about 20% against the pound limits the net impact, and the company is not a market maker on Scotch prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of R&O in West Bengal and how is the market structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulatory approvals are the last step and are expected this quarter; the company would return to the market about 60 days later. Management does not see the market turning unfavourable.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth can be achieved without capex, and at what utilisation is new capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no plans for new ENA/ethanol capex beyond maintenance of INR50-60 crore a year; utilisation guidance is about 85%. Capacity is seen flat through FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net debt and manufacturing margin trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt was INR650 crore against INR660 crore in March 2026. Manufacturing margin is within INR5-7 per litre and management is not concerned about changes in that range.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the IMFL brand mix shift across states, with some brands rising and others falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said brand growth varies by state because category mix differs (vodka, semi-premium and deluxe whisky markets). It said no brand is structurally declining and this will continue as the company enters new geographies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UP ramp-up path and what is the margin outlook for R&O?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify quarterly UP additions but said UP is the next big bankable R&O opportunity, with a FY29 guideline already set.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company balance volume growth, input inflation and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing margin is protected by FCI fixed-price supply, maize hedging, and monthly pass-through in the flexi-price E&A business. P&A is self-funded from cash flow, with no further capacity expansion planned.

risks_watch: Glass and PET cost-push of 10-17% may squeeze R&O margins if pass-through lags.
Q2 agri inflation for broken rice (unhedged) and maize, plus the eastern India rainfall deficit.
West Bengal R&O re-entry depends on pending regulatory approvals; timing has slipped before.
P&A still loss-making at EBITDA level (negative INR13 million) and needs to reach profitability.
UP R&O mix is lowering margins toward 15-16%, and UP internal versus external sales mix is still being optimised.
Branded IMFL brand-level volatility across states; repeat behaviour for Mountain Oak and Brothers & Co. was questioned by analysts.
Ethanol overcapacity in the industry and policy ambiguity around E20 and higher blends.
summary.management_tone: Confident on manufacturing and UP growth, with specific numbers and guidance reiterated. More guarded on timelines for West Bengal approvals, Bihar policy, UK FTA benefits and UP quarterly growth, where management declined to quantify.
key_quotes: Q1 has been a good start to the year.
Manufacturing is not a passive capacity business for us; it is an active operating platform.

The P&A business is not going to continue to grow in a manner where expenses are growing faster than revenue from approximately 60% or so negative margin a couple of years ago, we are now at nearly at breakeven.
We are firmly within that in Q1.

growth.why: No new capacity is planned (no ENA/ethanol additions through FY29, maintenance capex only of INR50-60 crore a year) and no numeric revenue growth guidance was given; the quarter's 13% revenue and 33% EBITDA growth is backed by record 89% utilisation, R&O/UP volume scaling and P&A volume growth of 45%, with margin bands (INR5-7/litre manufacturing, 15-17% R&O) held.
